Subject: Hypercube GPU slate: proposed lifecycle & activation cadence

Ava —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together three proposal tracks for a dedicated reservation tailored to Hypercube's inference profile. The attached PDF has the math, but the short summary is below.

Key constraints you flagged: model peak tokens/session (~1.2k), a mix of synchronous low-latency (user-facing) and async batch work, and an expected 3x Q4 throughput increase tied to new product features. You also need predictable unit economics for budget planning and a canary plan for rollout.

Option A — Compact steady-state
- Cluster: 16 A40-equivalent GPUs (single AZ)
- Min guarantee: 12 GPUs (baseline SLA for 99th pct latency targets)
- Ramp: 100% available at T+0 (fast onramp)
- Fit: teams that need consistent latency and limited burst
- Pros: easiest billing predictability; lowest coordination overhead

Option B — Staged ladder (recommended for Hypercube)
- Cluster: 32 A40-equivalent GPUs across 2 AZs
- Min guarantee: 18 GPUs (keeps user-facing SLOs during normal hours)
- Ramp schedule: Week 0: 18 GPUs; Week 4: +6 GPUs; Week 12: +8 GPUs -> full 32
- Burst windows: configurable hot burst lanes + preemptible extension for non-critical batch jobs
- Fit: predictable growth with rollback points and canary lanes

Option C — High-burst runway
- Cluster: 48 GPUs (multi-AZ) with 20 GPU min guarantee and 28 burst pool
- Ramp: conservative two-month warmup and phased activation to validate model ops
- Fit: customers prioritizing headroom for unpredictable spikes

Operational notes common to all options:
- Canary plan: we recommend a 4-node canary pool pinned to the new model version for 7 days before broad traffic shift.
- Warmup credits: we can include a small warmup credit (token-based) during the first 30 days to defray compilation and KV-cache priming costs.
- Failover: automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-cost quantized model variant if queue latency exceeds configured thresholds.

Attached: detailed cost/throughput table and the activation cadence workbook for your team to tweak the Week-by-week increments.

Next steps: if you like Option B, we can produce a formal commitment term sheet and a proposed onboarding timeline for legal/procurement. Can we sync Thursday 11am PT to walk the workbook?

Thanks,
Jonas

2) For the burst pool in Week 12, what are the expected per-token costs compared to the reserved baseline? We want to model costs in our chargeback.

Ava — quick answers inline, and added a small update to the workbook to include the latency sims.

1) Latency (18 GPU baseline) — 99th pct
- Using your profile (1.2k tokens, mixed sync/async) we simulate median ~ 85ms, 95th ~ 160ms, 99th ~ 270ms when the baseline hosts user-facing lanes exclusively. Those numbers assume continuous KV-cache priming and workload-aware batching.
- If you mix batch jobs onto the same lanes, expect 99th to drift toward ~350ms during heavy concurrency. That’s why we recommend separating user-facing lanes (min guarantee) from batch pools.

2) Burst pool pricing — high-level
- Reserved baseline per-token: $0.0014 (example for committed pricing; final depends on term length)
- Burst (on-demand capacity) per-token: approximately +40–55% relative to reserved baseline during peak windows
- We can instead offer a blended bursting rate if you want predictable chargeback (we have a blended option used by other customers).

I've uploaded a small simulation tab to the workbook (activation_cadence_workbook.xlsx) with the latency rows and blended-cost column. I also attached a short Appendix B that lays out the assumptions.

If Thursday still works, Marissa will run the workbook walk and Karthik will cover rollout and canary orchestration.

Best,
Jonas
